questions.problem:
A triangle $S$ has vertices at $(4,1),(0,-3),(-1,3).$  Which of the following are coordinates of the vertices of ${S}^{′},$ the image of $S$ under the **clockwise** rotation ${R}_{-{180}^{∘}}$ by an angle of ${180}^{∘}$ about the origin?

- $(1,-3)$
- $(-4,-1)$
- $(0,3)$
questions.worked_solution:
The clockwise rotation ${R}_{-{180}^{∘}}$ by an angle of ${180}^{∘}$ is the same as counterclockwise rotation by the same angle. It's given by the matrix

$$
R=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}].
$$

To find the image of $S$ under the action of ${R}_{-{180}^{∘}},$ we first create a matrix $X$ containing all of the vertices of $S:$

$$
\begin{aligned}X & =[\begin{aligned}4 & 0 & -1 \\ 1 & -3 & 3\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we compute the image of $X$ under ${R}_{-{180}^{∘}}$ by calculating the matrix product $RX:$

$$
\begin{aligned}RX & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}4 & 0 & -1 \\ 1 & -3 & 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-4 & 0 & 1 \\ -1 & 3 & -3\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the coordinates of the respective vertices of ${S}^{′}$ are $(-4,-1),(0,3),(1,-3).$

So, the correct answer is "I, II and III."

Example: 
                    Using a Matrix That Represents a Rotation of 90 Degrees
canonical_examples.problem:
A triangle $S$ has vertices at  $(-5,-1), (1,4), (3,-5).$ Which of the following are coordinates of the vertices of $S',$ the image of $S$ under the **clockwise** rotation $\mathbf{R}_{-90^\circ}$ by an angle of $90^\circ$ about the origin?

- $(1,-5)$

- $(4,-1)$

- $(-5,-3)$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
The clockwise rotation $\mathbf{R}_{-90^\circ}$ by an angle of $90^\circ$ is the same as counterclockwise rotation by an angle of $270^\circ.$ It's given by the matrix

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14122491/assets/7f8b60362b08e038452b3454b1719c6f51df7d0129cc7d957e328a92b4f7e7c3.svg)

To find the image of $S$ under the action of $\mathbf{R}_{-90^\circ},$ we first create a matrix $X$ containing all of the vertices of $S$ as columns:

$$
\begin{aligned}X & =[\begin{aligned}-5 & 1 & 3 \\ -1 & 4 & -5\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we compute the image of $X$ under $\mathbf{R}_{-90^\circ}$ by calculating the matrix product $RX\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}RX & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ -1 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-5 & 1 & 3 \\ -1 & 4 & -5\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 4 & -5 \\ 5 & -1 & -3\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the coordinates of the respective vertices of $S'$ are $(-1,5), (4,-1), (-5,-3).$

So, the correct answer is "II and III only."

Let's define a linear transformation ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14122491/assets/5ab4d8d28ee7c7e99d35b1f9932f168e9311ecc0ca1dc0e494fdf73fa1baf484.svg) by its standard matrix ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14122491/assets/c2c85081d1f89d74b8ebb2761496d211d7052193809b7864e7983437f5d0b80f.svg) given by 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14122491/assets/c6865c5373231451885b3d76e3c8151e9c707462a8b405d9b014b1bda17065a8.svg)

We can find the images of ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14122491/assets/a7655c84c060c79a0c0850d5d0537e4b4d7b7826d0339e261f87aa7ed4f09229.svg) under ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14122491/assets/5ab4d8d28ee7c7e99d35b1f9932f168e9311ecc0ca1dc0e494fdf73fa1baf484.svg) by computing the matrix products, as follows:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14122491/assets/5b8e1c8e03ebb60716eaa2fefded5e7fc286f6de9cffdece8200f6f56c2bbe8e.svg)

Plotting the vectors ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14122491/assets/1f249f835230ce9561402247b4c94e15cae46adc5e7dc4263316da3bfcf2348a.svg) and ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14122491/assets/bcfcd6164292fee1aeff0dc8325607fc44ff8fe3fa41d4d3abfb95c17d98db92.svg) and their images ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14122491/assets/e5f0a5e6b245b18ea6c8d6f65c82702cba528e740aacd5e97535e5705cea9415.svg) and ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14122491/assets/982d513f1246c98c5055421fad26619b5fe53085da40a017673554f8c992631d.svg) we obtain the following:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14122491/assets/c2dc9f76bb23225cec0a4f62541d8a74c4c4b16d2e2f7c37e8d36922d97c59f0.png)

We see that the transformation ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14122491/assets/5ab4d8d28ee7c7e99d35b1f9932f168e9311ecc0ca1dc0e494fdf73fa1baf484.svg) represented by the matrix ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14122491/assets/3207697e43e4f88223ad85c16964c3103a50c0c999a4ca14417695158d45526b.svg) defines a **counterclockwise rotation of ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14122491/assets/a3bf307d258c37da47916be4e50553ef612072912cd6ed8dc24fddafc6c3722a.svg) (or ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14122491/assets/8662109ab709179527b5d1768c0f42a8fb4d6493e41082c5317be360ec4169dd.svg) radians) about the origin.**

Note that we typically refer to rotations in the counterclockwise sense. However, in this case, the transformation ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14122491/assets/5ab4d8d28ee7c7e99d35b1f9932f168e9311ecc0ca1dc0e494fdf73fa1baf484.svg) can also be considered a rotation of ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14122491/assets/a3bf307d258c37da47916be4e50553ef612072912cd6ed8dc24fddafc6c3722a.svg) (or ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14122491/assets/8662109ab709179527b5d1768c0f42a8fb4d6493e41082c5317be360ec4169dd.svg) radians) *clockwise* about the origin.
